newsitem.title: USA: Rubin expected to stay as Treasury chief - sources.
newsitem.headline: Rubin expected to stay as Treasury chief - sources.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin is expected to remain on the job now that President Clinton has won a second, four-year term, sources close to Rubin said on Wednesday.

Rubin, who is widely admired in financial markets for his astute handling of the economy, told reporters last week that he had no plans to return to Wall Street although he stopped short of saying that he would stay on at Treasury.
Rubin worked at Wall Street broker Goldman Sachs before joining the government in 1993 as head of Clinton's National Economic Council. He became Treasury chief two years later.
